column1: # Per-module wall clock for the hub TLA+ gate, in seconds, on a GitHub
# ubuntu-latest runner (4 vCPU; TLC takes -workers auto, so this is a
# 4-worker number and will not match an 8-core workstation).
# Read by scripts/tla-shards.sh to balance the job matrix. A module
# absent from this file falls back to run-count times 30s, so the file
# is an optimisation and never a correctness requirement: a wrong number
# costs an unbalanced shard, never a skipped run.
# this gate ever executed on Linux, and it did not finish. It was killed
# by the job timeout after 120 minutes having completed 183 of 246 runs,
# so a THIRD OF THE GATE HAS NEVER BEEN TIMED ANYWHERE. Those modules are
# marked NOT MEASURED below and carry the fallback estimate. Regenerate
# this file from a full green run and the guesses go away.
# The number that decides the shape of the matrix: ForgeSync.cfg is a
# SINGLE run (2960 s on 2026-09-30, 4576 s on 2026-10-03). No partition of
# this gate can finish faster than that, at any granularity, until that
# model is made cheaper; ForgeSync is split into its runs (below) so that
# run is all its shard holds.
